texts.preamble: Sagiruddin vs State Of U.P. on 18 October, 2019 Author: Rajeev Misra Bench: Rajeev Misra High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad Court No. - 28 Case :- Criminal Revision No. - 985 of 2002 Revisionist :- Sagiruddin
texts.facts: The shop of the revisionist was inspected by Chief Food Inspector on 9.2.1993 at 10 a.m. As according to Food Inspector, the revisionist was not having any licence in respect of food items sold by him, a complaint was filed in Court of Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Court No. 2, Allahabad. On this account, trial stands vitiated.
texts.arguments: Learned counsel for the revisionist contends that in the present case, all the incriminating material and adverse circumstances were not disclosed to the accused under section 313 Cr. P. C. It is then submitted that the accused has been convicted under Sections 7 (3) and 16 (1) (a) (ii) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954. Elaborating his submissions he submits that Section 7 (3) reads as follows:- "7. Prohibitions of manufacture, sale, etc., of certain articles of food.--No person shall himself or by any person on his behalf manufacture for sale, or store, sell or distribute-- (i) any adulterated food; (ii) any misbranded food; (iii) any article of food for the sale of which a licence is prescribed, except in accordance with the conditions of the licence; Referring to the word prescribed used in sub Section 3 of Section 7, he submits that word prescribed used in aforesaid Section shall be meant to be prescribed by rules, therefore, in order to record the guilt of the revisionist under section 7 (3) of Food Adulteration Act, 1954, it was incumbent upon the Trial Court to record a finding as to under which Rules, requirement of licence was mandatory and was not possessed by the revisionist. He then submits that conviction of revisionist under Section 16 (1) (a) (ii) of Sagiruddin vs State Of U.P. on 18 October, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50479499/ 2 Food Adulteration Act, 1954 is also illegal. Section 16 (1) (a) (ii) refers to punishment for selling such food articles, which are adulterated. In the present case, there is no report of any laboratory pointing out that food items sold by revisionist were adulterated. It is thus urged that conviction awarded by the Court below is manifestly illegal and hence liable to be [LEAKAGE_MASK] by this Court. Learned A.G.A. has contradicted the submissions urged by the learned counsel for the revisionist. However, learned A.G.A. could not place before the Court the provisions or Rules under which licence is required for food items be sold by Revisionist who is a general merchant. Learned A.G.A. could not make such submissions on the basis of which submissions made by the learned counsel for the revisionist could be discarded.
